How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide that walks you through creating a **RESTful GET** request against the *Cisco Nexus Dashboard* (v6.3.1) to pull the “Device Connector Versions” data set. I’ll cover both the **web UI** approach (the built‑in API console) and a **code‑first** approach (cURL / Python). --- ## 1️⃣ Using the Built‑In API Console (Web UI) | Step | What to do | Why | |------|------------|-----| | **1. Log into the Dashboard** | `https:///` | You need admin/reader credentials that allow API access. | | **2. Go to the “Developer” → “API Explorer”** | Click the gear icon → “API Explorer” | This opens the interactive console where you can browse all available endpoints. | | **3. Find the “Device Connector Versions” endpoint** | Search “device connector versions” or look under the “Device Management” group | The endpoint will look something like `/api/v1/device_connector_versions`. | | **4. Expand the endpoint** | Click the arrow next to it | You’ll see the supported methods; click **GET**. | | **5. Set the required headers** |
  • `Authorization: Bearer `
  • `Accept: application/json`
| The token can be generated via the “Generate Token” button in the console. | | **6. Add optional query params** | If you want to filter by device ID, add `device_id=` | Filters reduce payload size. | | **7. Hit “Send”** | The console will display the raw JSON response | You can copy/paste this into your own scripts or save it as a file. | > **Tip:** The console automatically shows the full request URL, so you can copy it for later use. --- ## 2️⃣ Using cURL (Command Line) ```bash # Replace placeholders: # – e.g., nexus-dashboard.company.com # – JWT or OAuth token obtained from the UI # – optional filter curl -X GET \ https:///api/v1/device_connector_versions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -G \ --data-urlencode "device_id=" ``` - `-G` tells cURL to append the data as query parameters. - Omit the `--data-urlencode` line if you don’t need filtering. The response will be a JSON array of objects, each representing a connector version record. --- ## 3️⃣ Using Python (`requests`) – Quick Example ```python import requests BASE_URL = "https:///api/v1" ENDPOINT = "/device_connector_versions" TOKEN = "" DEVICE_ID = "" # optional headers = { "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}", "Accept": "application/json", } params = {"device_id": DEVICE_ID} if DEVICE_ID else {} response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}{ENDPOINT}", headers=headers, params=params) response.raise_for_status() # raises exception on non-200 status data = response.json() print(data) # pretty‑print or process further ``` > **Note:** In production you’d probably wrap this in a function, handle pagination, and store the result in a database or CSV. --- ## 4️⃣ Common Pitfalls & How to Fix Them | Issue | Symptom | Fix | |-------|---------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | “Invalid token” | Regenerate token in the UI or refresh your session. | | **404 Not Found** | Endpoint missing | Verify you’re on the correct API version (`/api/v1/…`). | | **Rate limiting** | 429 Too Many Requests | Add exponential back‑off or throttle your calls. | | **Large payloads** | Slow responses | Filter by `device_id`, `status`, or use pagination (`page=1&size=100`). | --- ## 5️⃣ Next Steps 1. **Save the request** – In the API console, click the “Download” button to export the request as a cURL command or Postman collection. 2. **Automate** – Schedule a cron job or Azure Function that runs the Python script daily and writes the output to a CSV or database. 3. **Visualize** – Feed the JSON into Grafana or Power BI for real‑time dashboards. That’s it! With those steps you can pull the “Device Connector Versions” data from Cisco Nexus Dashboard v6.3.1 at any time. Happy querying!
